title: Build an interactive 3D view
summary: Build a 3D model scene, fit its camera, and add direct interaction.
outcome: A framed 3D model with interactive controls.

blocks.text: Rotate, inspect and frame a model
Build a small model viewer in three stages: place two meshes, orbit around them, then pick a model and change its surface. Each stage keeps camera input and object state easy to inspect.
The first version places a `Box` and `Sphere` under one perspective camera. Set `Camera.fov` explicitly in radians and look toward the origin before judging the models’ scale.
Mesh resolution determines geometric detail. `Material.color` determines surface appearance. Change the sphere segments and then its color to compare those responsibilities.
2. Explore the scene with an orbit camera
The second version adds `OrbitCameraController`. Drag empty space to orbit and use the wheel to change distance. The models remain in their original positions.
Orbiting is a camera interaction. Object transforms and material state belong to the models, so viewing a different side should not secretly rotate or recolor them.
The final version installs `InteractionManager`. Hovering supplies a subtle emissive cue; clicking a model switches its roughness between matte and glossy settings.
Each handler invalidates the scene after changing material state. Try clicking each model separately: their shared scene does not mean they share the same material values.
Use it in your own application
Keep expensive mesh rebuilding out of pointer-move handlers. Change material or transform state for ordinary interaction and rebuild topology only when the shape actually changes.
Dispose the scene and its controllers when replacing the canvas. Decide whether application state should survive that replacement before reconstructing entities.
